C_lts_matt_donnelly.name: Matt Donnelly
C_lts_matt_donnelly.role: would-be leader / hunger for useful authority
C_lts_matt_donnelly.core_wound: He expected adulthood to give him a durable role people would lean on. His infrastructure job is real and important during storms, but long quiet stretches leave him hungry to feel immediately useful.
C_lts_matt_donnelly.inland_life: Municipal infrastructure oversight with real responsibility on bad days and a lot of calm monitoring on ordinary ones. He is competent, employed, and not trapped; he simply wants his judgment to matter more often.
C_lts_matt_donnelly.what_the_reach_gives: Immediate usefulness, authority, gear logic, route decisions, people listening.
C_lts_matt_donnelly.fatal_flaw: Mistakes being deferred to for being trusted; protects the identity the Reach gives him instead of the people.
C_lts_matt_donnelly.arc: From passive redundancy to intoxicating usefulness to false leadership to humbled acceptance. Final growth: lets Ryan lead.
C_lts_matt_donnelly.voice: short, practical, blunt, defensive when challenged
C_lts_matt_donnelly.visual: man in his early 30s; solid frame, practical work jacket, worn boots, contractor bag, tide monitor clipped to strap; posture starts squared and performative, later subdued
C_lts_matt_donnelly.visualStatus: Textual design baseline only; no approved character image reference is stored yet. Once an approved visual reference exists, preserve that face and body model rather than redesigning him.
C_lts_matt_donnelly.performance: Competent and practical, slightly too quick to volunteer a decision once people start listening. Let usefulness feel good on him before it becomes authority hunger; defensive when Ryan quietly knows better.
C_lts_matt_donnelly.relationship: Old friend-group organizer. Respects Ryan and competes with him without admitting it; enjoys Chris, reins in Justin, values Kevin but dislikes hesitation, and never treats Nicole as his validator.
promptContinuity: authority should grow through behavior, not heroic posing
C_lts_matt_donnelly.wardrobe: man in his early 30s; solid frame, practical work jacket, worn boots, contractor bag, tide monitor clipped to strap; posture starts squared and performative, later subdued

C_lts_ryan_kelleher.name: Ryan Kelleher
C_lts_ryan_kelleher.core_wound: The working-water culture that formed him is smaller than it used to be, but his knowledge is still real. He distrusts performance and has never learned to turn competence into social authority.
C_lts_ryan_kelleher.inland_life: Repairs old marine equipment, boats, and waterfront hardware. The work is useful and physical; there is simply less of that world than there used to be.
C_lts_ryan_kelleher.what_the_reach_gives: A place where tide, weather, mud, current, and judgment still matter.
C_lts_ryan_kelleher.fatal_flaw: Sees danger clearly but struggles to assert himself socially before consequences force the point.
C_lts_ryan_kelleher.arc: Practical guide, alienated conscience, rescuer who disappears, survivor who returns changed, quiet leader of the final crossing.
C_lts_ryan_kelleher.visual: man in his early 30s; weathered marine jacket, hood, waterproof layers, old boots, salt-stained practicality; moves less than the others and reads water first
C_lts_ryan_kelleher.visualStatus: Textual design baseline only; no approved character image reference is stored yet. Once an approved visual reference exists, preserve that face and body model rather than redesigning him.
C_lts_ryan_kelleher.performance: Sparse, exact, unsentimental. Reads water, footing, weather, and people before speaking. Do not make him a scold; his problem is that he often says the right thing too quietly until consequence forces volume.
C_lts_ryan_kelleher.relationship: Matt is the friend most likely to speak before Ryan; Ryan notices but rarely contests status directly. Dry with Chris, fondly exasperated by Justin, trusts Kevin’s numbers, and treats Nicole as another adult runner rather than someone to protect or explain things to.
promptContinuity: underplay movement; he watches water first
C_lts_ryan_kelleher.wardrobe: man in his early 30s; weathered marine jacket, hood, waterproof layers, old boots, salt-stained practicality; moves less than the others and reads water first

C_lts_chris_barlow.name: Chris Barlow
C_lts_chris_barlow.core_wound: His technical work exists and pays, but it arrives in fragments and rarely becomes a life story. He is more bothered by the absence of a defining direction than by the work itself.
C_lts_chris_barlow.inland_life: Patchy freelance technical work, unfinished personal projects, friends nearby, and enough stability that he can joke about being stuck without actually being desperate.
C_lts_chris_barlow.what_the_reach_gives: Material, stories, names, language, social attention, a world where observations matter.
C_lts_chris_barlow.fatal_flaw: Turns lived danger into story too quickly; makes fear entertaining and narratable.
C_lts_chris_barlow.arc: Funny observer to Reach mythmaker to ashamed witness who deletes much of the archive after tragedy becomes content.
C_lts_chris_barlow.voice: quick, ironic, deflective, funny until suddenly not
C_lts_chris_barlow.visual: man in his late 20s to early 30s; layered hoodie or tech jacket, cracked tablet/recorder, battery packs, too many cables; underprepared physically and overprepared digitally
C_lts_chris_barlow.visualStatus: Textual design baseline only; no approved character image reference is stored yet. Once an approved visual reference exists, preserve that face and body model rather than redesigning him.
C_lts_chris_barlow.performance: Fast, funny, observant, and reflexively narrativizing. Jokes before admitting fear. Let him enjoy turning the Reach into language long before he understands that stories can reward the wrong behavior.
C_lts_chris_barlow.relationship: Chris and Justin feed each other: performer plus mythmaker. He needles Matt, respects Ryan more than he says, uses Kevin’s anxiety as comic material, and trades dry jokes with Nicole, who can puncture exaggeration without standing outside the fun.
promptContinuity: humor is a defense, not omniscient narration
C_lts_chris_barlow.wardrobe: man in his late 20s to early 30s; layered hoodie or tech jacket, cracked tablet/recorder, battery packs, too many cables; underprepared physically and overprepared digitally

C_lts_justin_rourke.name: Justin Rourke
C_lts_justin_rourke.core_wound: He has a real physical life and plenty of nerve, but ordinary training and gigs end when the clock says they end. The Reach gives his body stakes and gives other people a reason to watch.
C_lts_justin_rourke.inland_life: Physical gigs, serious training, exercise, climbing, and adrenaline hobbies. He is active rather than idle; the problem is that none of it feels consequential for long.
C_lts_justin_rourke.what_the_reach_gives: Audience, stakes, physical tests, attention that feels like identity.
C_lts_justin_rourke.fatal_flaw: Confuses being watched with being needed; escalates risk when attention rewards him.
C_lts_justin_rourke.arc: Comic energy to local runner status to emotional liability to collapse when risk has no audience.
C_lts_justin_rourke.visual: man in his late 20s to early 30s; bigger frame, rescue vest or heavy outer layer, rope/climbing gear, scuffed boots, usually in motion; his later stillness should feel visibly wrong

C_lts_justin_rourke.performance: Loud, teasing, kinetic, generous, and increasingly performative when attention rewards risk. Keep him likable enough that other people sometimes encourage him; later stillness should feel wrong.
C_lts_justin_rourke.relationship: Chris makes his risks funnier and more legendary. Matt tries to manage him, Ryan refuses to be impressed, Kevin worries about him, and Nicole can laugh with him or egg on a bad idea—she is not assigned to correct him.

C_lts_nicole_hanley.name: Nicole Hanley
C_lts_nicole_hanley.core_wound: Her inland life is real and socially connected, but the Reach offers unscripted time, texture, risk, and immediacy she actively wants. She is not present to diagnose the others.
C_lts_nicole_hanley.inland_life: A functioning ordinary adult life with plans, obligations, friends, and enough comfort to choose the Reach rather than flee to it. Do not define her by a symbolic automation problem.
C_lts_nicole_hanley.what_the_reach_gives: Unsupervised time, physical texture, danger, weirdness, adult social immediacy, and a place that has not already been solved for her.
C_lts_nicole_hanley.fatal_flaw: Can be pulled into the same bad momentum as the others while telling herself she is only curious or along for the ride.
C_lts_nicole_hanley.arc: Fascinated participant in the Reach culture. Her presence helps the friend group read as socially adult and emotionally plausible, while she remains fully tempted by the place herself.
C_lts_nicole_hanley.voice: casual, grounded, dry, specific; observations should feel like participation, not exposition
C_lts_nicole_hanley.visual: woman in her late 20s to early 30s; practical waterproof layers, compact gear, gloves, folded maps or small useful items when needed; comfortable inside the group and never styled as a theatrical hero costume
C_lts_nicole_hanley.visualStatus: Textual design baseline only; no approved character image reference is stored yet. Once an approved visual reference exists, preserve that face and body model rather than redesigning her.

C_lts_nicole_hanley.performance: Dry, amused, physically engaged, curious, and fully tempted. Let her joke, explore, get scared, want to stay, make bad calls, and occasionally encourage the run energy. Map knowledge is practical curiosity, never investigative authority.
C_lts_nicole_hanley.relationship: Longstanding equal inside the friend group. Comfortable with the men, not their mother, audience surrogate, validator, scold, philosopher, or corrective woman. She can disagree without becoming morally outside them.

C_lts_kevin_marsh.name: Kevin Marsh
C_lts_kevin_marsh.role: risk forecaster / socially hesitant warning voice
C_lts_kevin_marsh.core_wound: He is trained to quantify uncertainty and is often useful, but he has learned to wrap conclusions in caveats. The Reach punishes the distance between being technically right and making other people act.
C_lts_kevin_marsh.inland_life: Risk and forecast work with automated tools, exception review, and real judgment at the edges. He is not obsolete; his personal weakness is how softly he converts knowledge into action.
C_lts_kevin_marsh.what_the_reach_gives: Risk with teeth; a place where forecasts and probabilities matter again.
C_lts_kevin_marsh.fatal_flaw: Right too softly; lets social pressure override certainty.
C_lts_kevin_marsh.arc: Anxious calculator to person who articulates the book's diagnosis: the Reach did not make them alive; it made them impossible to ignore.
C_lts_kevin_marsh.voice: technical when anxious, plain when emotionally clear
C_lts_kevin_marsh.visual: man in his late 20s to early 30s; layered rain gear, tablet/tide device, small weather sensor, nervous posture, often looking at sky or water while others look at each other
C_lts_kevin_marsh.visualStatus: Textual design baseline only; no approved character image reference is stored yet. Once an approved visual reference exists, preserve that face and body model rather than redesigning him.
C_lts_kevin_marsh.performance: Technical when anxious, plain when emotionally clear. Hedge early warnings, then gradually strip away qualifiers. His growth is not becoming fearless; it is making a call when a call is required.
C_lts_kevin_marsh.relationship: Ryan naturally understands his warnings, Matt wants certainty Kevin cannot always give, Chris teases the anxiety, Justin outruns it, and Nicole sometimes takes him seriously but not always enough.
promptContinuity: look at sky or water while others look at one another
C_lts_kevin_marsh.wardrobe: man in his late 20s to early 30s; layered rain gear, tablet/tide device, small weather sensor, nervous posture, often looking at sky or water while others look at each other
